  ✓ .worktrees/, left empty
  ✓ .gitignore: `.worktrees/` and `.ticket-runner/`, with the comments `init` wrote them under
  ✓ docs/agents/, left empty
  ✓ ticket-runner.json

GitHub:
  ✓ the `in-progress` label, from every issue that wore it
  ✓ the `ticket-runner/state` branch
  ✓ the `ticket-runner/lock` branch

Left for you:
  label `needs-triage`: Planning uses it too — `gh label delete needs-triage` removes it
  label `needs-info`: Planning uses it too — `gh label delete needs-info` removes it
  label `ready-for-agent`: Planning uses it too — `gh label delete ready-for-agent` removes it
  label `ready-for-human`: Planning uses it too — `gh label delete ready-for-human` removes it
  label `wontfix`: Planning uses it too — `gh label delete wontfix` removes it
  merge settings: squash merging and deleting a pull request's branch when it merges are left as they are, since this repository may have had them before `init` — `gh repo edit --enable-squash-merge=false` or `gh repo edit --delete-branch-on-merge=false` turns one off
  branch `agent/12-some-title` on GitHub: pull request #40 is open on it
  branch `agent/9-another-title` on GitHub: no pull request is open on it
  issue #88: the standing Notes issue, left open with the Notes on it
  #12, #15: no Run can resume them any more, because their State files, and any hand-off transcripts kept beside them, went with `ticket-runner/state`
  comments on issues: the progress, hand-off and Note comments Runs wrote are left as they are, since they are addressed to humans
  nothing was committed: review the changes with `git status` and commit them yourself

Done: the pipeline has gone from this Target.

On stdout, and exit code 0. The first line names the Version doing the removing
(ADR-0007), in the shape `init-report.txt` gives its own.

Three groups, always in this order and always all three, however little each has
to say; an empty one says `  nothing to remove`.

`Removed:` is what went from the Target's working tree, one line per item, each
marked `✓` or `✗`. The config file, the conventions document and the Operator's
skill go whatever they say, because they are the pipeline's own text. The
`CLAUDE.md` section and each `.gitignore` entry go only where they are still
exactly the text `init` writes, and a `CLAUDE.md` or `.gitignore` left holding
nothing else goes with them:

  ✓ CLAUDE.md: deleted, because the section `init` wrote was all it held
  ✓ .gitignore: deleted, because the entries `init` wrote were all it held

`.ticket-runner/` goes whole. Each `ticket-<n>` worktree goes with the branch it
has checked out, and every other local `agent/` branch after them. `.worktrees/`
goes only when that leaves it empty, and its `.gitignore` entry only then too.
A directory another removal left empty goes, named `left empty`; one that was
empty before, or still holds anything, stays. The config file goes after every
other removal, the ones in `GitHub:` included, and before only the lock branch:
it is the only place a renamed label is named, so where a removal failed it
stays, and the next run looks for the label and the Stranded Tickets under the
names it gives.

`GitHub:` is the in-progress label, by the name the config gives it, which
GitHub takes off every issue wearing it, closed ones included; then the
`ticket-runner/state` branch; and last of all the `ticket-runner/lock` branch,
which this command held the whole time so no Run started while it worked.

A removal that fails is marked `✗`, with git's or GitHub's reason, and the rest
carry on:

  ✗ docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: EACCES: permission denied, unlink '<path>'

The lock branch is then released rather than deleted, in the line that takes its
place in `GitHub:` and again in the last group, and the command exits 1:

  ✓ the Run lock, released to free

Running it again is a first run over what is left.

`Left for you:` is what the pipeline cannot prove it put there, or leaves on
purpose, each line with what to do about it:

- the five triage labels other than in-progress that the Target has, which
  Planning uses too, each with the command that deletes it
- the two merge settings `init` switches on, which the repository may have had
  before it
- each `agent/` branch on GitHub, and the pull request open on it, if any: they
  are a Ticket's work
- the standing Notes issue, by number, which is addressed to a human
- the Tickets whose State files went with the state branch, which no Run can
  resume any more, and the hand-off transcripts that went with them. They are
  read before the branch is deleted, and a branch whose Tickets cannot be read
  is kept and marked `✗`, so none of them goes unnamed
- the comments Runs wrote on issues, which are addressed to humans
- whatever of the pipeline's stays because it no longer matches `init`'s text,
  or shares a directory with something else:

  CLAUDE.md: the section pointing at docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md is not the text `init` writes, so it stays
  .gitignore: `.worktrees/` stays, because it is not under the comment `init` writes it with
  .worktrees/: holds scratch besides the pipeline's worktrees, so it stays, and so does its `.gitignore` entry
  ticket-runner.json: kept, because a removal above failed and it names the labels the next `ticket-runner remove` looks for — that run deletes it with the rest
  ticket-runner/lock: released rather than deleted, because a removal above failed — `ticket-runner remove` again deletes it with the rest

- a reminder that nothing was committed, whenever the working tree changed:
  like `init`, `remove` leaves the change for the human to review and commit

A line GitHub could not be asked for says so, and changes no exit code:

  branches on GitHub: could not be listed — <reason>

The last line is the exit code in words: `Done: the pipeline has gone from this
Target.` for 0, and `Not done: <n> removals failed — run `ticket-runner remove`
again to remove what is left.` for 1. A Target with nothing to remove and no lock
branch takes no lock and ends `Nothing to remove: ticket-runner has not set this
Target up.`, with exit code 0.

On a terminal, without `-y` or `--yes`, the command asks before it removes
anything, once the refusals below have passed and it holds the Run lock. The
opening line comes first, then what it is about to remove and the question. A
`CLAUDE.md` that holds nothing but the section is listed as
`CLAUDE.md, because the section `init` wrote is all it holds`.



ticket-runner <version> remove · <repo root>

About to remove:
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md
  .claude/skills/ticket-runner/SKILL.md
  CLAUDE.md: the section pointing at docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md
  .ticket-runner/
  .worktrees/ticket-12, and its branch agent/12-some-title
  agent/7-other-title, a local branch
  .gitignore: the entries `init` wrote
  any directory this leaves empty
  the `in-progress` label
  the `ticket-runner/state` branch
  ticket-runner.json
  the `ticket-runner/lock` branch

Remove all of this? Nothing will be committed. [y/N]

`y` or `yes`, in any case, goes on to the report above. Anything else releases the
lock and ends on stderr, exit code 2:

Nothing was removed. Run `ticket-runner remove` again when you want it gone.

Every refusal is one message on stderr, exit code 2, nothing changed, in this
order, and each says what to do next:

1. A shell carrying the Stage mark, before anything is read, as `init` refuses it.
2. A cloud Host, which can delete no branch (ADR-0008):

Refusing to remove on a cloud Host: it can delete no branch on the remote, so the Run lock and State branches would stay. Run `ticket-runner remove` on a workstation instead.

3. A `gh` that cannot speak to GitHub, in the words `init` uses:

Refusing to remove: `gh` is not authenticated — run `gh auth login`, then `ticket-runner remove` again.
Refusing to remove: `gh` is not installed — install the GitHub CLI from https://cli.github.com, then `ticket-runner remove` again.

4. A conventions document a newer Version stamped:

Refusing to remove: 0.6.0 set this Target up and this is 0.5.2, so it may have left things this Version does not know to remove. Upgrade with `npm install -g "github:jjongs2/ticket-runner#semver:*"`, then run `ticket-runner remove` again.

5. Neither a terminal nor `--yes`:

Refusing to remove: there is no terminal to ask whether to go ahead. Run `ticket-runner remove --yes` to remove without asking.

6. A Run lock anybody holds, named as `stop` names it, and never taken over:

Refusing to remove: `ticket-runner run` (run <runId>, pid <pid>) holds the Run lock on this Host, started <startedAt>. Wait for it to finish, or ask it to with `ticket-runner stop`, then run `ticket-runner remove` again.
Refusing to remove: `ticket-runner run` (run <runId>, pid <pid>) holds the Run lock, but its process on this Host has gone. `remove` takes over no lock: start `ticket-runner run` to take it over and finish what it held, or commit a `lock.json` that reads `{ "held": false }` to the `ticket-runner/lock` branch, then run `ticket-runner remove` again.
Refusing to remove: `ticket-runner run` (run <runId>) holds the Run lock from <the workstation `<hostname>` | the cloud Host of session `<session>`>, started <startedAt>. Wait for it to finish or, if it is gone, commit a `lock.json` that reads `{ "held": false }` to the `ticket-runner/lock` branch, then run `ticket-runner remove` again.

Then the command takes the Run lock itself, recording its own command line. The
last two refusals release it to free before they exit:

7. A Stranded Ticket, an open issue wearing the in-progress label:

Refusing to remove: #12 and #15 still carry the `in-progress` label, so they are Stranded Tickets a Run was killed holding. Finish them with `ticket-runner run`, or relabel them, then run `ticket-runner remove` again.

8. A `ticket-<n>` worktree holding work no commit on GitHub carries:

Refusing to remove: these worktrees hold work GitHub does not have, which removing them would lose:
  .worktrees/ticket-12: uncommitted changes
  .worktrees/ticket-15: commits its branch on the remote does not have
Push what is worth keeping, and take out a worktree nothing in is wanted with `git worktree remove --force <path>`, then run `ticket-runner remove` again.
